ai_enhancement.explanation: Root Gradle properties file for the Kotlin-based AxiSight Android project. Typically holds JVM memory settings (org.gradle.jvmargs), AndroidX flags (android.useAndroidX), Kotlin code style, and build cache/parallel execution toggles. No settings were parsed here, suggesting it is minimal or the parser could not extract values.
ai_enhancement.best_practice: Explicitly enable performance flags: org.gradle.caching=true, org.gradle.parallel=true, org.gradle.configureondemand=true. Pin android.useAndroidX=true and kotlin.code.style=official. Document any non-obvious memory tuning with inline comments.
ai_enhancement.security_concern: ✅ No secrets detected. Ensure no signing keystore passwords or API keys are ever placed here — gradle.properties is often committed to VCS.
ai_enhancement.migration_suggestion: Consider splitting machine-specific tuning into a non-committed ~/.gradle/gradle.properties and keep only project-portable settings in the repo copy.
ai_enhancement.context: Standard Gradle project configuration. Use the user-home gradle.properties for secrets/local overrides and the project file for shared build semantics.

* Detects the center of the darkest circular blob in an image.
 *
 * Algorithm (over the downscaled target region):
 *   Pass 1 — luminance grid cache + histogram mean/σ → adaptive threshold = mean − kStd×σ,
 *             plus sharpness (Laplacian variance)
 *   Pass 2 — connected-component labelling of pixels ≤ threshold (4-connected). Each
 *             component gets a WEIGHTED centroid (weight = threshold − lum + 1, so darker
 *             pixels pull harder) and weighted 2nd moments → circularity. Components outside
 *             [minAreaPx, maxAreaPx] are discarded; of the rest the one with the best
 *             weight × circularity² wins. Scratches, shadows and debris next to the bore
 *             therefore become separate, losing components instead of smearing the bore's
 *             centroid and circularity (the earlier "all dark pixels" approach failed on
 *             real bores for exactly that reason).
 *   Pass 3 — contrast-ratio gate (chosen blob must be meaningfully darker than the region)
 *             and circularity gate on the chosen component
 *   Pass 4 — boundary refinement: casts rays out from the centroid, finds the
 *             sub-pixel threshold crossing on each, and fits a circle ([CircleFit])
 *             to those edge points. The weighted centroid is biased by lighting
 *             gradients across the blob; fitting the boundary instead is not, so
 *             this pass is used as the final center when it converges cleanly.
 *
 * [detectCore] is shared by the [ImageProxy] (YUV), [Bitmap] (ARGB) and NV21 overloads.
 * Per-thread scratch buffers are reused across frames, so steady-state detection allocates
 * nothing beyond the result object.
Reusable per-thread work buffers (detection runs on one thread per camera source).

* Three-layer temporal filter for detection results.
 *
 * Layer 1 — Jump filter
 *   If the raw detection jumps more than [DetectorConfig.maxJumpPx] from the last
 *   accepted position, the result is rejected and the consecutive streak is reset.
 *   This kills noise spikes and brief occlusions that produce implausible teleports.
 *
 * Layer 2 — Consecutive-frames gate
 *   Requires [DetectorConfig.consecutiveFramesRequired] successive successes (after jump
 *   filtering) before the first detection is published. A single failure resets the count.
 *   This kills single-frame glitches, partial occlusions, and startup transients.
 *
 * Layer 3 — Adaptive EMA + dead-band
 *   Once the gate is cleared, position is smoothed with an EMA whose alpha scales upward
 *   with velocity: slow-moving tool → heavy smoothing (low jitter); fast-moving tool →
 *   lighter smoothing (fast response). A sub-pixel dead-band prevents micro-jitter from
 *   dirtying the readout when the tool is stationary.
 *
 * [reset] must be called whenever the camera source changes or tracking is stopped.

* USB (UVC) camera fragment built on AUSBC's [CameraFragment].
 *
 * Detection runs on the camera's raw NV21 preview frames (delivered by libuvc through
 * [IPreviewDataCallBack]) rather than on screenshots of the preview TextureView: no GL
 * read-back, no ARGB conversion, full camera frame rate, and — because the frame is in
 * camera image space — the shared [FrameAnalyzer] maps results through the app-wide
 * CoordinateMapper exactly like the internal camera, so calibration captured on USB is
 * stored in image space too.

 * Frames arrive on libuvc's thread. Each one is handed to a dedicated processing
 * thread; if that thread is still busy the frame is dropped (keep-latest), so a slow
 * detection never backs up the camera.
